items.title: National Grid says a viral 19 November blackout warning is fake
items.summary: A mocked-up post claiming parts of the UK would lose power from 4pm on Thursday 19 November was shared tens of thousands of times. National Grid says no outage is expected and asks people to report the post and rely on official channels.

items.title: Cable faults cut power to homes across Lancashire and Greater Manchester
items.summary: SP Electricity North West said underground cable faults caused outages on Tuesday morning in places including Saddleworth, Irlam, Blackpool and the Ribble Valley, with up to about 280 homes off in each area. A snow warning was in force at the time.

items.title: Lords committee warns the UK is badly prepared for emergencies
items.summary: The National Resilience Committee says limited stockpiles leave Britain exposed to cyberattacks and extreme weather, and warned a cyberattack could quickly turn into a power cut. It wants a Cabinet minister just for resilience and welcomed the Be Ready campaign.

items.title: BBC reveals its emergency radio plan for a national blackout
items.summary: The BBC has a 'Black Sky' plan to keep broadcasting on FM radio for at least 72 hours if the power fails nationwide. The government says there is no specific threat to the grid.

items.title: Low wind triggers a grid warning for tight supplies
items.summary: The grid operator NESO warned supplies would be tight on Monday 9 November as weak winds cut generation, then cancelled the notice. It is the seventh such warning this year, against one in 2025.

items.title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 homes without power
items.summary: Around 160,000 homes lost power at the peak and two men were killed by falling trees. About 90,000 were still off supply that evening.
